R001.name: Hardcoded Secret
R001.description: Sensitive credentials stored directly in source code.
R001.impact: Attackers may extract secrets from repositories or deployed applications.
R001.fix: Store secrets in environment variables or secure vault solutions.

R002.name: SQL Injection
R002.description: SQL query constructed using string concatenation.
R002.impact: Attackers may manipulate database queries and access unauthorized data.
R002.fix: Use parameterized queries or ORM frameworks to prevent injection.

R003.name: Command Injection
R003.description: System command executed using potentially unsafe input.
R003.impact: Attackers may execute arbitrary system commands on the host machine.
R003.fix: Avoid passing user input directly into system commands. Use safe APIs or validate input.

R004.name: Weak Cryptography
R004.description: Use of weak or deprecated cryptographic hash function.
R004.impact: Weak algorithms like MD5 or SHA1 can be broken, allowing attackers to compromise data integrity.
R004.fix: Use strong hashing algorithms such as SHA-256 or bcrypt.

R005.name: Insecure Deserialization
R005.owasp: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
R005.description: Use of unsafe deserialization method such as pickle.
R005.impact: Untrusted serialized data may execute arbitrary code during deserialization.
R005.fix: Avoid using pickle for untrusted data. Use safer formats like JSON.

R006.name: Logging Sensitive Data
R006.owasp: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
R006.description: Sensitive data is written to logs or console output.
R006.impact: Sensitive credentials may be exposed in logs or console output.
R006.fix: Avoid logging sensitive information or mask the data before logging.

R007.name: Insecure Error Handling
R007.description: Application is running with debug mode enabled.
R007.impact: Debug mode may expose sensitive system information and stack traces.
R007.fix: Disable debug mode in production environments.
